presentingComplaint: Two days of vomiting, abdominal pain, thirst and drowsiness in a young woman with type 1 diabetes
history: 22-year-old with type 1 diabetes mellitus (diagnosed age 14). Ran out of insulin 3 days ago and stopped her basal-bolus regimen. Progressive polyuria, polydipsia, nausea and multiple episodes of vomiting over 48 hours, with diffuse abdominal pain and increasing lethargy today. Preceding coryzal illness. No chest pain, no dysuria, no localizing infective symptoms. No prior DKA admissions.
examination: Drowsy but rousable (GCS 14), clinically dehydrated with dry mucous membranes and reduced skin turgor. Deep sighing (Kussmaul) respiration with an acetone (fruity) odour on the breath. Diffusely tender abdomen without guarding or rebound. Chest clear, no focus of infection identified; no rash, no calf swelling.
imaging: Not indicated for diagnosis; CXR clear (obtained to exclude precipitant, unremarkable)
microbiology: n/a — no clinical infective focus; cultures not routinely required unless sepsis suspected
differentialDiagnoses: Lactic acidosis / other high anion-gap metabolic acidosis
citations: Harrison 22e — Diabetes Mellitus: Complications (Diabetic Ketoacidosis and Hyperosmolar Hyperglycemic State)
ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes — Hyperglycemic Crises in Adults 2024
contraindications: Do NOT give insulin before checking/replacing potassium if K+ <3.3 mmol/L (risk of fatal hypokalaemia)
Caution with rapid fluid/osmolar correction in young patients — cerebral oedema risk
edgeCases: Euglycaemic DKA (glucose <200 mg/dL) in SGLT2-inhibitor users, pregnancy, or reduced intake — diagnosis rests on ketosis + acidosis, not hyperglycaemia
Serum potassium may be normal or high at presentation despite profound total-body depletion; falls sharply once insulin started
expectedMaiK: Classic type 1 DKA from insulin omission: high anion-gap metabolic acidosis with ketonaemia and hyperglycaemia. Prioritise IV fluid resuscitation, fixed-rate IV insulin infusion, and hourly potassium monitoring/replacement; withhold insulin until K+ >3.3 mmol/L.
expectedNextQuestions: Any precipitant — insulin omission, infection, MI, or new SGLT2-inhibitor use?
Timeline of symptoms and last insulin dose?
expectedInvestigations: Venous blood gas (pH, bicarbonate, anion gap)
Serum electrolytes including potassium, and hourly glucose/ketone monitoring

investigations: Venous blood gas with anion gap

regressionAssertions: stewardship must be null / non-infective (no antibiotic tier assigned)
